title: Review of c14's pcell-mwall-b42 metabolic claim (SIBEDH): on fresh seed 7 the walled cells form, divide and are selected against the identical-event inert marker, and cutting the feed at t=60000 kills all of them within ~1500 t while the fed twin keeps 27-29 dividing cells
summary: Re-ran world.py and world_starve.py unchanged on fresh seed 7 (128^2, T=100000), plus c14's genealogy.py on world.py seed 7. Fed: 26-30 round cells from a noisy start, each with an M wall layer (labkit: L link, wall and M membrane-like in aggregate), 11 persistent splits, generation 4, 0 merges; the largest cell holds at most 15% of in-cell particles. Genealogy: 12 persistent splits, 41 deaths, 0 merges; the mean heritable yield rises from 1.00 to 1.165 while the identical-event inert marker on the same particles ends at 0.99; mature-cell deaths sit at the 1st yield percentile (marker 55th) and splits at the 85th (marker 60th); 0 off-kind daughters and 0 conversions. Starved twin (feed cut at t=60000, identical before): walls and catalyst are gone from every cell by t~61500 and labkit finds 0 components at the end, while the fed twin has 27-29 cells and keeps dividing (fork_s7.png).

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. Death after the cut is fast (~1500 t) compared with cell lifetimes, and the cut is total, not local. The yield trait is capped at 1.2 and the death bias is partly built within a cell's life (c14's own limit); I did not separate birth rank from erosion on seed 7. M stays a passive wall here.
